abstract:
  "Evidence accumulation models (EAMs) decompose response time and accuracy data from speeded decision-making tasks into latent cognitive parameters, including the rate of evidence accumulation, response caution, and non-decision time. This tutorial introduces three EAM implementations available in the bmm R package — the EZ-Diffusion Model (EZDM), the Censored-Shifted Wald Model (CSWALD), and the Diffusion Decision Model (DDM) — and demonstrates how to fit them to empirical data using a unified Bayesian hierarchical framework. We first cover data preprocessing, including contaminant detection and summary statistic computation, using bmm's dedicated helper functions. Four tutorials then build progressively: Tutorials 1 and 2 demonstrate the EZDM with three and four parameters using aggregated summary statistics. Tutorial 3 transitions to trial-level modeling with the CSWALD in both simple (censored) and competing-risks versions. Tutorial 4 fits the full DDM using the Wiener first-passage time likelihood and compares estimates across all three model families. Complete R scripts accompany each tutorial. After completing the tutorials, readers will be able to select an appropriate EAM for their data, fit it using bmm, and evaluate and interpret the results."
